recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli (Pasta and Beans)
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup ditalini or other small pasta
1 (15 ounce) can cannellini beans, with liquid

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add onion, celery, garlic, parsley, Italian seasoning, pepper flakes, and salt; cook and stir until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth, tomato sauce, and tomatoes. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add pasta and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in undrained beans and cook until heated through, 3 to 4 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta e Fagioli (Pasta and Beans)
raw_recipe.description: Pasta fagioli is a traditional Italian soup with pasta and cannellini beans in a tomato broth. Serve with garlic bread for a hearty, comforting meal.

video.description: When the weather is cold, there’s nothing better than a warm bowl of homemade soup. In this video, Nicole shows you how to make pasta e fagioli (pasta and beans) that’s even better (and cheaper!) than the kind at Olive Garden. As its name suggests, this traditional Italian soup is made with cannellini beans and ditalini pasta along with vegetables, chicken broth, and tomatoes. It’s hearty enough to serve as a main dish at lunch or dinner, but it can be served as a tasty appetizer or side dish too. Make sure to top each bowl with freshly grated Parmesan cheese, cracked black pepper, and fresh parsley!

review.reviewBody: Four and a half stars. Husband really liked it. These are the changes I made: used a full 32 oz. of Kitchen Basics original chicken stock. One can Italian-style stewed tomatoes instead of tomato paste. I also added about 5-6 oz of frozen chopped spinach (thawed and squeezed dry) to the sauteed onions, garlic and celery. I think this added to the texture and heartiness of the soup. As far as seasonings so, I added about 3/4 tsp of salt and about 1/4 tsp freshly cracked black pepper; also a dash of chipotle Tabasco. Kept the crushed red pepper as we like spicy food. Boiled pasta separately as per several reviewers' suggestions (thanks for that, by the way) and ladled soup over this in individual bowls. It really didn't even need cheese on top. Great flavor, low fat, wonderful way to eat some vegetables and get some fiber with the beans. Thanks for an easy soup recipe that I'll be happy to make several times this fall and winter.
Please don't waste your time blanching and chopping tomatoes. A 14 oz. can of petite diced tomatoes works just as well and makes things a lot easier.

Loved it! Use full container chicken broth or veggie broth, 2 cans diced Italian tomatoes, cook in instapot. Used cheese filled tortellini- boil it first. Place in bowls and pour soup over top. Serve with crusty warm bread!

I made this and loved it. Very simple. Next time I will double the recipe. I made some changes because I didn't have everything on the list. I used veggie stock i/o chicken, I double the liquid due to comments I read, I used ditallinni pasta. I used 3 tablespoons of tomato paste i/o of 8 oz of sauce. At the end I also added spinach to add some nutrition and also use up some spinach I had in the fridge. It all turned out great.

This was a wonderful recipe. I made this with dry Cannellini beans (not canned) and added a little fresh spinach to the soup at the end. It all amounted to a soup that will certainly grace our dinner table for many Fall and Winter seasons to come. Served with a homemade French Baguette made the meal savory and satisfying. We also cook the pasta separately, adding some to the bowl and ladling the soup over it to keep the pasta from absorbing too much liquid and retaining its al dente texture.

I really liked this recipe! It was easy peasy to make, had ingredients I had on-hand, and took very little effort since my Meijer store carries onions, celery, and carrots in a container together already chopped and ready to go! I did mince my garlic myself! I made the pasta separately and placed it at the bottom of our pasta bowls and ladled the soup on top. I used authentic Italian shell pasta al dente and it was magnificent with the soup! Thick and just a little chewy as the perfect compliment to the tomato and beans! Plus, this is on our Mediterranean/DASH diet plan, so no guilt!

I always use a bit of salt pork in my recipe. I rinse it off first to remove residual salt. Cut into small pieces and slightly brown it. Then add celery (no onions) herbs, garlic and cook till just fragrant over low heat so the garlic doesn't burn. I add 1 large can of diced tomatoes and a can of water. I use white beans (rinsed first) and let it simmer for 2 hours. Add any small pasta you like.

This was a great base recipe for creating a delicious soup. I made some changes: used 32 oz. organic chicken broth, used canned Italian-style diced tomatoes (with onions, basil, and thyme), traded the spinach pasta out for orzo (which I boiled before adding to the broth), used kidney beans (without liquid) instead of cannellini, added garbanzo beans, and stirred in some spicy turkey sausage (because I wanted this to be meaty). Because the sausage was spicy, I didn't add the red pepper flakes and I didn't add any salt, since the broth had enough sodium. I shredded and added about 1/2 c. baby spinach, as well. It is pretty fantastic and I'll definitely revisit this recipe!

My family loved this with my adjustments: I used "ground" red pepper (I added less, we don't like it to hot), and "canned" diced tomatoes with garlic + onion instead of fresh tomato. I also "doubled" the recipe (got big eaters) so I put one can cannellini beans and one can small red kidney beans. I also added fresh baby spinach and shredded carrotts (cut up smaller). I cooked up one lb ground beef and one lb ground sweet Italian sauceage (sauteed onion, + celery with it). Served it with fresh baked bread. Although my favorite is the Olive Gardens pasta fagioli and I was hoping this would taste like theirs (but it didn't), I gave it four stars mainly because this is a good basic recipe. Will definiately make again, just might make a few more adjustments on the spices. A very hearty soup!

My nonna Giulia, rest her soul,made a similar Pasta eFagioli (pasta and bean soup), although her version called for a small bulb of fennel...no celery. Slice and fry the fennel in butter before adding it to the broth. Delicious.

I just made this and if not for the method, this would have got 5 stars from me hands down. The saute time takes 10 minutes not 5. Simmering took 40 for the celery to be tender enough. The only changes I made was using Vegetable broth because my daughter is Vegetarian, and I used small shell pasta. Everything else was exactly as written. This soup is amazing. So easy to make and so full of flavor. If you don't like your foods too spicy, cut down on the red pepper, It was perfect for us as is. We liked the spice. I am going to make double batches of this next time, so I can freeze some. If you do freeze, don't add the pasta. Add that after you thaw and reheat. 
Final rating: Method 4 stars, Flavor 5+ stars
I didn't change a thing! Perfect
love it and I live alone so itis just enough for me!

This is how I make it, and yes it is delicious, there is only one thing I do differently and that is to boil the pasta separately....I am making this tonight and will try just adding it. I think it is probably a game changer to make it a week night quick meal, and it is probably more creamy. For those who want to drain the beans, I say, please try it with the liquid. The liquid is what really makes the soup - Vegetarians know the liquid is creamy gold! I always use ditalini, which is what my mom always used and for some reason it's not pasta Faggioli if it isn't Ditalini (ditali)! I too, like others here, often start with a little bit of sausage or pork product that I brown first then the veggies do the job at deglazing the pan and the flavor is a boost, but I do agree that it isn't necessary - also my moms minestrone is this plus vegetables, so you can't get more simple than that!
I’ve been making it that way for over 50 years, but I do usually put either some smoked ham or some Italian sausage but as was said, it really doesn’t need it.
I make this recipie all the time. So quick and easy, and always a hit with dinner guests. Good as a side or as a main dish along with a salad.

My mother-in-law is the queen of simple cooking. When I first had this dish at her house, I was amazed by how delicious it was and couldn’t wait to recreate at home. Using only ingredients we already had at home, I made this simple, easy recipe—and my kids loved it. Now, it’s a staple in our weekly rotation, a comforting reminder that the best meals are often the simplest.
I also add turkey sausage. and some chopped kale. A sprinkle of oregano instead of the Italian seasoning. Added fresh parsley as a garnish. This makes a wonderful soup for a cold winters eve.
